newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks stay firm, end tad higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks stay firm, end tad higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed fractionally higher in strong turnover Thursday, defying a downward correction on Wall Street for the second day running and posting their ninth consecutive gain.
"The market looks good and it's managed to pry itself apart from Wall Street, partly thanks to strong local economic growth indicators," said Leonardo Torres Barsati, senior analyst at Rio Reserach.
The blue-chip MerVal index inched up 0.1 percent to end at 765.42. It gained 5.7 percent in the previous eight sessions and now stands at a five-year high.

Private consultants FIEL Wednesday predicted April industrial output rose 7.9 percent from the same month last year and 7.6 percent in the first four months of the year compared to the same period of 1996.

"It's always good when the bolsa performs a mild-mannered advance, although the tone will remain cautious for medium-term positions because U.S. investors still have good reason to think inflation will pick up and the Federal Reserve will eventually raise rates again," Barsati said.
The broad market closed flat, with winners outpacing losers 36 to 22 and 18 issues closing flat.
Floor volume firmed to 33.9 million pesos from 31.6 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter deals rose to 133.3 million pesos from 114.6 million Wednesday.
Top main-tier risers were real estate developer Irsa, oil company Astra and construction stock Juan Minetti, which gained 3.4 percent, 2.5 percent and 2.2 percent, respectively.
The weakest MerVal stocks were holding company Perez Companc, petrochemical concern Indupa and textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which shed 1.7 percent, 1.5 percent and 1.4 percent, respectively.
